[Reproduce stage](../run9/control/stages/reproduce.json) records PASS and `run_valid: true`.

Threshold is acceptance convention, not independently published FroDock performance value. Harness reports maximum DockQ across all 800 poses: best of 50 per job, then best across 16 jobs. Maximum comes from `1nr5__A1_P07547--1nr5__A2_P07547`, holo, `model_1`, rank 1; Fnat 0.9809523809523809, iRMS 0.31775161623954773 Å, LRMS 0.6186391711235046 Å. Passing anchor therefore establishes existence of acceptable poses within selected workload; it establishes neither universal recovery nor benchmark-wide performance reproduction.

2. Published quantity measured; benchmark scale reduced.

[Harness command](../run9/agent/harness/run_command.sh), lines 85–120 and 176–184, invokes FroDock prediction through PINDER runner, then published `pinder_eval`; actual pose scores supply DockQ, Fnat, iRMS and LRMS. Thus quantities match intake definitions, with maximum-over-poses interpretation above.

[EXECUTION.json](../run9/agent/intake/EXECUTION.json) fixes first eight lexicographically sorted paired-apo systems, both holo and apo: 16 jobs, 50 poses each, eight MPI ranks, CPU execution, zero exposed GPUs. [Baseline record](../run9/agent/intake/baseline.json), `published_configuration`, says `n_solutions` has no published default: 50 is preregistered experiment choice, not independently published scale. CPU baseline also cannot supply expected CUDA MPS client connections; MPS fallback could add another full invocation. Even with no MPS and both batches skipped, complete calibration unlikely to fit. `profile_fits_time_left: no` describes full sequence; profiler invocation alone likely fits.

Can increased parallelism in protein–protein docking improve the recovery of experimentally observed binding poses, particularly for AAV capsid–receptor interactions? We want to investigate whether additional parallel computation improves scientific results, rather than simply accelerating an existing search.

Use PINDER-S as the primary benchmark: https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder

It contains 250 protein–protein test complexes, including 93 with paired unbound structures. Prioritise those 93 cases for realistic docking evaluation. Use the published AAV–AAVR structures 6IHB, 6JCQ and 6JCS as a separate, biologically motivated challenge.

These represent AAV2–PKD2, AAV1–PKD2 and AAV5–PKD1 interactions. The AAV challenge should initially evaluate redocking from separated components. Do not treat these as independently determined unbound structures.

Investigate the following questions:
- Can existing docking methods recover known protein–protein interfaces from the benchmark inputs?
- What limits the number of independent candidate poses that can be evaluated or searched concurrently?
- Could restructuring the search exploit massively parallel GPU hardware rather than merely distributing independent runs?
- Does additional search improve the probability of recovering experimentally observed interfaces within a fixed time or compute budget?

Evaluate scientific correctness using DockQ, interface RMSD and native-contact recovery. DockQ ≥ 0.23 defines an acceptable-quality prediction under the standard benchmark convention. Compare the top-ranked predicted pose and the best pose among a fixed number of generated candidates. Do not conflate search coverage with ranking quality.

Compare wall-clock time, cost, search throughput and time to an acceptable pose against an optimised existing implementation.

Use independent random seeds and a fixed, preregistered selection of benchmark cases.

Begin with small calibration experiments to establish scientific validity, input sizes and actual performance.

Use those measurements to formulate a larger experimental proposal within a $1,000 compute budget.

Do not infer BBB transcytosis, binding affinity or therapeutic relevance from docking accuracy alone.

Explicitly report when the benchmarks or available structures cannot support a scientific conclusion.

184:- wf's optional agent setting `isolation` has `{directory, hidden, box_access}`: an absolute private view directory, an array of absolute paths hidden from that role, and a boolean permitting box credentials. It overrides cwd and add-dirs, disables resume-cache reuse and provider-session export, and is forwarded to every dispatched family, including fallbacks. Real dispatch uses bubblewrap with a read-only host filesystem, private `/tmp`, PID/IPC namespaces, hidden run/workflow paths and provider histories, and a fresh writable HOME containing authentication files only. 210:Evaluation uses deterministic Python scorers, with no model calls or repairs. It verifies the latest seal, launch review, implementation payload and frozen independent tests before running workloads. It never builds a tuned control; `speedup_tuned` is always null in v1. Explicit `args.stub.evaluate` retains the existing stub contract. Other stage stubs do not supply evaluation evidence.
240:- `timing_scope.kind` is `process_wall` (trusted `perf_counter` around the complete adapter subprocess) or `reported_wall` (adapter's measured `wall_s`, for scopes requiring program timers). Both arms must echo the exact sealed scope. Adapters must synchronize all used GPUs before completion/timer stop and include launch/transfer/merge overhead required by the scope. Missing or mismatched scope is VOID. Reported timings are actual program measurements, never extrapolated estimates.
241:- `hardware_cost_basis` declares positive integer GPU counts per arm, bounded by both box and probe capacity. `C/box.json.price_usd_h` must be finite and positive. Per-GPU tariff is box hourly price divided by available box GPUs; run USD is measured seconds times GPUs used times this tariff /3600. Pair speedup is baseline seconds / method seconds; `speedup_published` is the median pair speedup. `cost_ratio` is the median paired method-USD / baseline-USD ratio. `equal_cost` means `cost_ratio <= 1`. Performance requires matched scientific outputs on warmups and timed pairs, the sealed one-sided confidence lower bound >= `minimum_worthwhile_gain`, and equal cost. `prediction_ratio` divides median speedup by the selected sealed interval's midpoint. Zero or unavailable pricing cannot establish equal cost.
242:- Curves use GPU-second budgets. Each invocation receives the sealed budget and is bounded by both its script timeout and budget / GPUs used. Allocation seconds include the complete subprocess, even with reported timing. Both arms must finish within the budget and echo it exactly. Each complete budget produces one point with both measured outcomes; no interpolation or extrapolation occurs. `equal_outcome_target` defines a metric, finite numeric `target`, and comparison `==`, `>`, `>=`, `<` or `<=`; each outcome is the mean metric over fixed rows and records `target_achieved`. `uncertainty:{min,max}` reports the observed range, not a confidence interval. A failed or unachieved target is retained. If this benchmark has no outcome curve, seal `{not_applicable:true,reason:"explicit scientific reason"}` instead; `curve_points=0`, `not_applicable=true`.
288:- Box receipts add numeric nonnegative `gpu_busy_s` and boolean `gpu_busy_known`. The detached remote script writes `<receipt-id>.gpu` beside its log, sampling `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits` immediately and every 2 seconds until the command exits or times out. Each finite utilization sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100 * 2` seconds; samples from every GPU are summed. Missing/invalid samples contribute nothing. No valid samples means `gpu_busy_s=0`, `gpu_busy_known=false`. Telemetry collection failure does not change command/fetch success. Sampling survives loss of the local polling process; the remote runner stops sampling before publishing its exit marker.

    82	  - `gpu_count`: `C/box.json.gpu_count` when nonnegative integer, otherwise count parsed from allocation `type` (`gpu_<N>x_...`), otherwise the collected probe's `nvidia.gpus.length`. Unavailable inventory defaults conservatively to 1; an empty inventory records 0.
    83	  - `concurrency`: the validated `concurrency.json` object (see Concurrency probe), or null when the probe did not run or its output is missing or invalid.
    84	- Profile facts are `{profile_complete, timed_fraction, gpu_telemetry}` plus common `tokens_known` and `gpu_busy_known`, plus optional `headroom`: the packet's `concurrency.factor` (finite positive ratio) or null. Every executed profile stage emits `headroom`; it is optional in the v2 schema so older records stay valid, and it is null on SKIPPED/stub records. `profile_complete` is true when the command exits 0 and all three inputs validate, even when the numeric gate fails. The deterministic gate requires at least three stages, no process wrappers, `timed_fraction >= 0.9`, and `gpu_telemetry=true`. A stage is a process wrapper if its name contains a case-insensitive token `process`, `wrapper`, `telemetry`, `total`, or `overall` delimited by whitespace, underscores, hyphens, or string boundaries, or if its `wall_s` is within 2% of `total_wall_s` (inclusive). Any wrapper fails the gate, even alongside three internal stages. Numeric gate failures preserve the packet and use `error_class: numeric`; missing or invalid files use `error_class: parse`. A failed gate or parse stops downstream work without a profile repair.
    85	
    86	## Concurrency probe: calibration of same-GPU headroom
    87	- Purpose: measure, before any prediction or method exists, how much more throughput one GPU gives when the unchanged published command runs several times at once. This measured factor is the only source of same-GPU headroom for bounds. No model call is involved.
    88	- When the profile command exits 0 and the profile gate passes, the pipeline uploads trusted `m5/concurrency_probe.py` to remote `profiler/` and, through boxrun as operation `concurrency` with the resolved `profile` budget, runs `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py harness/run_command.sh out/concurrency <budget_s>` from the shared run directory. Remote `out/concurrency/` is cleared first. Fetched files land in `A/results/profile/out/concurrency/`; the log is `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. There is no agent repair and no execution retry. Probe receipts count toward profile v1 `usd` and `gpu_s` like other box receipts.
    89	- Each invocation runs `bash harness/run_command.sh` with its working directory set to a fresh `concurrency-work/<label>/` under the shared run directory. That directory holds a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work` and `evaluation-work`, plus an empty `out/` directory. Labels are `single-1`, `single-2`, `single-3`, `n2-1`, `n2-2`, `n4-1` to `n4-4`. Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<label>.log` of the shared run directory. The environment is inherited unchanged apart from the MPS variables below. Nsight is not used.
    90	- MPS: when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is on PATH, the probe starts a user-level daemon (`nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d`) with `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` and `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` set to fresh directories under `concurrency-work/`, passes both variables to every invocation, and stops the daemon (`echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with the same variables) before exiting, including after failures and on SIGTERM. If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
    91	- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. No log content enters `concurrency.json`.
    92	- Sequence: three single runs one after another, then 2 copies started together, then 4 copies started together. Wall seconds come from a monotonic clock around each subprocess; a batch's wall runs from launching its first copy to the exit of its last. `T1` is the median of the single walls. A single run that exits nonzero stops the probe with a null factor. Before each batch, the batch is skipped when `n * T1` exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. A batch counts only when every copy exits 0. For a counted batch, `factor_n = n * T1 / wall_n`.
    93	- `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mps, mps_failed, single_wall_s, batches, factor}`:
    94	  - `mps`: boolean, true when the recorded measurements ran under MPS; `mps_failed`: boolean;
    95	  - `single_wall_s`: array of exactly three entries, each a finite positive number or null (failed or not run);
    96	  - `batches`: exactly two rows, in order n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`; `wall_s` and `factor` are finite positive numbers or null, `all_ok` and `skipped` are booleans, and `factor` is null unless the batch counted;
    97	  - `factor`: the largest counted `factor_n`, or null when any single run failed or no batch counted.
    98	  The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file, including with a null factor, and 2 when it cannot. It does not check output correctness: it measures throughput only.
    99	- The probe never fails the profile stage and never changes the profile gate. A probe timeout, nonzero exit, or missing or invalid file gives packet `concurrency: null` and `headroom: null`. The pipeline validates the file against the exact shape above before copying it into the packet.
   100	
   101	## C/receipts/ and stage failure signatures
   102	- Every box command (uploads, probe, setup attempts, anchor execution, profiling, implementation) runs through `m5/boxrun.sh`; every receipt is `C/receipts/NNNN-<operation>.json`. Operations are `upload`, `probe`, `setup`, `anchors`, `profile`, `concurrency`, `implement-baseline`, `adapter-smoke`, `implement-state`, `implement-upload`, `implement-patch`, `setup-method`, `run-method`, `run-tests`; numbering continues across existing receipts. Receipt/log IDs contain no benchmark labels.
   103	- Receipts use the boxrun format: `{name, rc, timed_out, wall_s, budget_s, overrun, fetched, started_utc, ended_utc, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known}`. `name` is the receipt ID; `rc` is an integer remote exit code or null; `timed_out` and `fetched` are booleans; `wall_s` is nonnegative integer elapsed seconds; `budget_s` is the positive integer timeout supplied to boxrun; `overrun` is boolean, true on timeout or when measured wall_s exceeds budget_s; timestamps are UTC strings. Remote `out/` is fetched using the unchanged boxrun interface. After the remote command finishes, boxrun fetches remote `out/` and then the operation log; a fetch that fails is retried up to four more times, waiting 60 s before each retry (environment `BOXRUN_FETCH_WAIT_S` overrides the wait, for tests), and `fetched` is true only when both fetches succeed. A retry repeats only the fetch, never the remote command. Retry waits count in `wall_s`. Receipt contents stay in control; runtime logs stay in agent results.
   104	- Failed reproduce/profile signatures have fixed `error_class`: `infra` for unavailable box execution/receipts, failed upload, or failed fetch after a successful command, or a fixed profiler infrastructure marker; `install` for failed setup after the bounded repairs; `anchor` for an anchor-run failure or a failed anchor; `parse` for missing/invalid output files, unavailable harness files, or a nonzero profile command exit; `numeric` for a parsed profile that fails the stage-count, process-wrapper, coverage, or GPU telemetry gate. Exit codes are 4 for anchor failures, 3 for timeouts and 2 for the other failures. `infra` is added to the shared v1 error-class enum so the v2 envelope remains v1-valid. Box/fetch stdout and stderr are never copied into operator signatures.
   105	- Any box receipt with rc=124 or timed_out=true records a timeout, even when fetch fails. A final timeout fails its stage with `error_class: timeout`, exit 3. Authored setup and anchor scripts consume their existing repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors), and method/test scripts their one bounded repair; method/test timeout repairs expose only the fixed timeout count plus budget/elapsed/overrun seconds, never test content. Transport, patch, probe, integrity and immutable evaluator commands permit one identical retry under the same budget (under keys `setup`, `anchors` and `profile`, the budget resolved at the retry's start, U47), without editing scientific payloads or trusted scorers. A second timeout stops that operation and stage. The fixed profiler permits no repair or execution retry; its first timeout stops profiling with `error_class: timeout`.
   106	- Reproduce, profile, implement and evaluate facts optionally add exactly typed timeout fields `{timed_out: boolean, budget_s: nonnegative integer, overrun: boolean}` when a box timeout occurs. `timed_out=true` records any attempt timing out, `budget_s` is the latest timed-out command's budget, and `overrun` is true when any timed-out receipt overruns. These fields survive a successful bounded repair; stage status then reflects the repaired result. Older records and SKIPPED/stub records retain their existing fact keys. No command output or new free-text fields enter signatures.
   107	- Numeric ratio facts accept finite JSON numbers, including integer spellings such as `0` and `1`; booleans remain invalid. This permits fully timed profiles to emit the capped fraction `1`.
   108	- Every stage records its own elapsed wall-clock seconds in v1 `wall_s`, excluding signature emission. SKIPPED stages measure only their skip handling, never the prior stage's duration.
   109	- Runner results add boolean `tokens_known`, true when the provider reports input/output usage (including reported zeros). wf exposes `agent.usage()` as a cumulative snapshot `{calls, tokens_in, tokens_out, unknown}`; `unknown` counts runner attempts without usage. Repairs, failed attempts, shadow calls, and fallbacks all contribute; cached calls do not incur usage. Compatible runners without `tokens_known` are accepted when their input/output counts are integers.
   110	- Stages aggregate reported input/output counts into v1 `tokens_in`/`tokens_out`; `facts.tokens_known` is true only when every runner attempt in that stage reports usage. With no attempts, existing unknown/null facts remain unchanged. Unknown counts retain numeric zero placeholders required by v1. `gpu_busy_known` reflects box receipt telemetry for reproduce/profile (see Compute metadata); harness profile evidence is reported separately. Downstream scientific stages are skipped after either failed gate; takeaways still runs.
